prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
For new_screen changes (2 tests), no clear effect was seen in either test.
The choose_path reorder change was helpful, winning Round 4 (+11.9% after noise correction).
The home redesign change was helpful, winning Round 6 (+3.6% after noise correction).
The sign_in reorder change was harmful (-6.1% after noise correction) and was stopped early.
Evidence is still thin for adoption (new_flow and redesign), choose_path, sign_in, and home redesign changes, as only one test of each kind has been completed.
Predictions were too high for tests with no clear effect or negative results, but underpredicted the major winning test in Round 4.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_flow: +0.2% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- adoption, redesign: -0.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, reorder: +11.9% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_screen: -1.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, new_screen: -3.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, redesign: +3.6% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -6.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 89.4%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 84.1%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 21.7%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, new_flow] Home Intro Control Primer Flow: Rebuilds the home intro welcome screen into a multi-step interactive flow demonstrating how to hide, drag, and talk to the pet. (why: Multiple support tickets report user confusion after onboarding on how to control or hide their pet, and finish step drops to 64.8%.)
1: [home, hint] Pet Generation Progress Time Estimate: Adds estimated completion time and clear progress status indicator on the waiting screen during pet generation. (why: The waiting stage has a median duration of 201s and a mean of 2336s, causing users to abandon the app believing it froze.)
2: [home, wait_info] Background Pet Generation Notification: Adds a desktop notification toggle on the waiting screen so users can minimize the app while generation finishes. (why: Waiting step mean time is over 38 minutes (2336s), showing users leave the screen open or idle while waiting.)
3: [finish, notification] Desktop Pet Interaction Banner Prompt: Adds a prominent highlight banner on the home welcome screen showing direct key bindings and taskbar control tips. (why: 3 support tickets reported users not knowing how to talk to or hide their pet after completing setup.)
4: [sign_in, copy] Sign-In Progress Preservation Messaging: Updates headline, body, and hint copy on sign_in screen to reassure users that signing in preserves their current pet progress. (why: Sign-in step drops conversion to 72.9%, and users express fear of lost or reset pets upon re-authenticating.)

scores.note: Addresses high finish drop-off with support ticket backing, but new_flow/new_screen changes historically showed no clear lift and require heavy build effort.
Directly addresses severe home waiting time (2336s mean) with low-overhead progress indicators to reduce drop-off.
Targeted at extreme home step delays by letting users minimize, supported by duration metrics.
Clear evidence from tickets and finish funnel drop-off; low cost UI banner prompt on existing screen.
High drop-off step (27.1% loss) backed by user feedback; simple copy change is cheap (cost 2) and directly resolves progress loss anxiety.
